industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying a view that moved inside the industry this week: Software B2B Enterprise goes to Neutral on the rotation into software, Semiconductors stays Underweight on the AI capital spending re-pricing, Hardware stays Neutral with the evidence moved against it at the margin. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the market has stopped paying for AI capital spending (hyperscaler prints gave no lift, ABB sold on data-centre orders) while demand is intact and sub-sector upgrades continue (memory, equipment, power electronics), and the software-against-semiconductors factor pair is reversing (Goldman Sachs' desk, 26 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, B prior. The industry row stays C because the industry is split by the rotation itself. Counter-case for D: the Nasdaq down 6% in two weeks with momentum down 15% is a regime statement about this industry; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Neutral, from Underweight, because the thematics read turned: the broadening trade has moved into software. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): Nordic software 'is working again', up 9% in a month as AI-disruption fears faded while hardware gives back gains (Danske Bank TMT, 27 October), and Goldman Sachs' desk (26 October) reports the software-against-semiconductors factor pair reversing, so two houses now describe the same rotation; against it the discount-rate case still holds (the US ten-year above 5%, the Fed hiking in December) and one software sector is not another (Fortinet down 20%, ServiceNow down 16%, cybersecurity broken; Outset Global, 29 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: A now, C prior, the market now ranks the sector first. Balanced, so Neutral by judgement, not Overweight: a row valued off a yield cannot be Overweight with the ten-year above 5%. Seven Pool names (Sinch and Sectra in the top twelve of the starting score, QT Group, Truecaller, Yubico, Planisware, SAP). Counter-case: the recovery is one month old in one region and the discount rate is rising. To B if the Fed path is marked down with relative strength holding A or B; back to D if relative strength falls to C with the ten-year still above 5%.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium. Hexagon (HEXA.B-SE) is a self-help case with a cyclical tailwind: a compelling business change at an uncompelling price. The park rule does not bite (management B; business quality B; predictability B; trackability C); the case is parked on the return, which fails the 20 percent bar at 98.56 SEK (2026-09-30) on the modal path (about -0.2 percent a year over eighteen months; about 4.2 percent a year over three years at a 20 times multiple) and on the bull's own multiple (6.3 percent a year at 22 times held; 12.9 percent a year at 24.1 times held). The case progresses at about 75 SEK on the modal path, or at about 82 SEK if the cleared-branch conditions (core organic growth at or above 6 percent and core gross margin above 63 percent through 2027) are both shown by then, which would move the fair multiple to 22 times. The next test is Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-23. The business is one to own below about 75 SEK; at 98.56 SEK the record is not betting on it, because the bet would be that the market goes on paying the software-rich Hexagon's multiple for the hardware-heavier company it has become.
case: The thesis. Hexagon is a self-help case with a cyclical tailwind: a compelling business change at an uncompelling price. In fourteen months a new chief executive has changed the people, the structure, the profit metric, the perimeter and the cost base, and the outputs have turned; at 98.56 SEK the shares, at 24.1 times earnings 24 months forward, already pay for that change and for the 2030 targets being met, so the modal return is about nil over eighteen months and about 4 percent a year over three years, and the case clears the 20 percent bar only below about 75 SEK.

The change is internal, broad and already delivered. An activist-prompted board replaced the chief executive and then the chairman; the new chief executive's Konecranes record is of exactly this playbook. Four fifths of the executive team changed; the matrix became seventeen divisions with their own profit and loss; the 74 million EUR cost programme reached a 73.5 million EUR run-rate two quarters early; Design and Engineering was sold for 2.7 billion EUR; Octave was spun off; net debt fell from 3,356 million EUR to 483 million EUR; the unmet 30 percent-plus EBIT margin target became a 24 to 26 percent EBITAC target for 2030, called "highly achievable" by the sell-side; EBITAC, which deducts capitalised R&D, replaced EBIT1. Nine of the framework's twelve internal forces are present and strong against a decision rule of three, and the screen's red flags are absent: a permanent operator, not a caretaker; a transformation in the numbers, not on slides; no crown jewel sold cheaply; leverage 0.6 times rising to 1.5 times against a 2.5 times ceiling; no debt-funded buyback. The one force that moved the wrong way is guidance, lowered to a reachable level, treated as a credibility gain rather than a change force. Internal forces rate A.

The external forces net to a modest tailwind that is cyclical in its largest parts (B). Defence and anti-jamming (GPS spoofing events over 1,000 a day), North American near-shoring (+20 percent organic in Q2 2026) and the artificial-intelligence electronics cycle (double-digit growth in Manufacturing Intelligence electronics; China +10 percent off a low base) carried the core to 12 percent organic growth in Q2 2026 against a 6.3 percent consensus. Those forces are small in the mix; the largest end-markets (automotive, 19 percent of Manufacturing Intelligence; construction, 45 percent of Geosystems; Chinese infrastructure, with high-speed rail construction down 85 percent; agriculture in deep recession) are still contracting. The company's own cycle troughed in Q1 2025 (organic growth 0 percent; a profit warning; adjusted margins down 380 basis points) and has turned: 3, 8 and 12 percent in the last three quarters; a two-quarter-old turn is a turn, not a cycle with visibility. Competition is tightening at the two edges (Chinese low-cost metrology at half the Western price; Trimble gaining 1 to 3 percent share in connected workflows; PTC discounting 60 to 70 percent) while the premium core (Hexagon, Zeiss, Mitutoyo) is stable. Currency is unhedged by policy. Demand B; political and regulatory B (defence up; tariffs passed through with a lag); competition, disruption, supply side, macroeconomic and the catch-all (the Octave flowback) C.
counter_case: The strongest case against the record's view is the bull case at full force: that the record anchors on a history that no longer applies in the other direction. The core is a 52 percent software-and-services business by the sell-side's wider definition, with 97 percent gross retention, a 26 percent EBIT1 margin, 149 percent cash conversion, a number-one global position in metrology and a chief executive who has beaten in every quarter since the targets were set. It grew 12 percent organically in a quarter in which Trimble grew 12 percent and Sandvik 15 percent, and the cost programme's full-year effect, Waygate's 16 percent-margin radiography and remote-visual-inspection core and the TS20 product cycle are not in a consensus that still carries the Octave strip-out in its six-month numbers. On that reading the multiple is not a legacy but the market pricing a simpler, faster, more honest company: DNB Carnegie's SEK 110 is a floor rather than a target, 22 times EBITAC is "undemanding", and a 20 to 25 times 24-month-forward multiple held on 10 percent-plus earnings growth gives 12 to 13 percent a year with upside if estimates keep rising. The evidence for it: the Q2 beat across every line; the cost run-rate; a higher backlog in all three segments; the three-month revisions; a historical 30 to 40 percent premium to the Stockholm market now at parity; and a record in which the company's crises have been "temporary valuation plateaus followed by deep, value-unlocking corporate transformations".

Against the 'Foundations': the core is a cyclical hardware company whose moat is narrower than its retention figure suggests. The 97 percent retention is measured on software accounts; the hardware that now dominates the mix is sold into automotive, construction and general manufacturing capital-spending cycles, two of which are contracting; the low end is being taken by Chinese makers at half the Western price; the software that is left lacks a unified cloud platform and loses collaborative projects to Dassault and Trimble; the Product Vitality Index fell from 10 percent to 6 percent, which says past R&D was partly mis-spent. On that reading the 'Foundations' are a C, and the twelve-percent quarter was a recovery from a destocking-depressed base in the small, fast ends of the mix, not a widening advantage.
triggers: - The entry price: about 75 SEK on the modal path over eighteen months (about 65 SEK over three years); about 82 SEK if organic growth at or above 6 percent and gross margin above 63 percent are both shown through 2027; about 90 SEK even at the current multiple held; about 70 SEK on the drop-through sensitivity.

- What would change the record's mind on organic growth: a Q3 2026 print below 8 percent organic with a lower backlog, or two quarters below 4 percent (alarm); a negative organic quarter outside a recession (invalidate).

- On the gross margin and mix: a core gross margin below 62 percent for two quarters refutes the mix thesis (the earnings review's own refutation level); above 63 percent confirms it; below 61 percent for two quarters invalidates.

- On the EBITAC margin: below 22 percent in any quarter (alarm); below 21 percent (invalidate); Manufacturing Intelligence EBITAC below 20 percent after Waygate (alarm); a second write-down or a synergy walk-back (invalidate).
- On the multiple: a year of 8 percent-plus organic growth with gross margin above 63 percent would make 22 times the floor rather than the ceiling; a fall in the multiple is the entry, not an alarm.
- On the end-market cycle and currency: a Western Europe organic decline with an adverse currency quarter (alarm); a group organic decline (invalidate).
